This is the public SDK surface of @pinstripe/sdk. Customers read these method names, so they follow the Stripe surface, NOT the repo's kit verbs.

## Method names
- Allowed verbs: list, retrieve, create, update, delete, cancel, void, finalize, pay, confirm, advance, reverse.
- Flag any kit verb here — findCustomers, getCustomer, fetch*, load*, save* — as a required change. This is the one place in the repo where `list` and `retrieve` are correct.
- Flag any method invented for a route that does not exist. A missing method is the real shape of the API, not an omission: entitlements has only `list`, products has no `delete`, creditNotes has no `void`.

## Paths
- Every resource declares exactly one `{DOMAIN}_PATH` constant and builds every path from it. Flag a repeated base path literal.
- Every path parameter goes through `buildPath` / `encodeURIComponent`. Flag raw interpolation.

## Types
- The response envelope stays visible in the return type — `Promise<ListResponse<CustomerResponse>>`, never unwrapped to `Promise<Customer[]>`.
- Domain types are re-exported through `src/types/contracts.types.ts` with `export type`, from `@pinstripe/core/contracts`. Flag a domain type declared inside the SDK.

## Imports
- Never import `@pinstripe/core` as a value — it lands in the bundle and `src/bundle.test.ts` fails. Type-only imports are fine.
- Never import a `node:` builtin outside `src/node/**`.
- Never read `process.env` outside `src/node/create-pinstripe-client.ts`.

React Query plumbing lives inside the SDK here, not in the consuming app.

- The subject enum is `PinstripeQuerySubjectEnum`. Flag `ReactQuerySubjectEnum` or a string literal used as a subject.
- Query keys come from `usePinstripeQueries()`, never from a module-level import — the `queryFn` needs the client instance from the provider.
- Hook names keep their suffix: `use{Entity}Query`, `use{Action}{Entity}Mutation`. Never define `queryKey` / `queryFn` inline; spread the factory entry.
- A mutation hook invalidates the related queries FIRST, then reports. Invalidate the singular key by id and the plural key by `._def`.
- Never import `sonner` or any toast library into the SDK. Report outcomes through the provider's `onMutationError` / `onMutationSuccess`.
- `MutationProps<TData>.successMessage` carries the text from the call site: a `string`, or `(data: TData) => string`. Passing nothing means no toast — silence is the default. Flag `shouldBeSuccessToast` or any Vietnamese string literal inside the SDK.
- A non-error outcome that needs reporting as one (a PSP decline surfacing as `paymentIntent.failureMessage`) does not belong here: the hook only invalidates, and the page branches via `mutate(vars, { onSuccess })`. Flag an SDK-constructed `PinstripeError` for a 200 response.
- Never read `process.env`, and never import a `node:` builtin.

`@pinstripe/sdk` is a published package with a bundle test guarding its boundaries.

- Never import `@pinstripe/core` as a value anywhere in `packages/sdk/src` — it enters the bundle and `src/bundle.test.ts` fails. Type-only imports are fine.
- Never import a `node:` builtin outside `src/node/**`.
- Never read `process.env` outside `src/node/create-pinstripe-client.ts`. The SDK knows exactly one env family: `PINSTRIPE_API_URL`, `PINSTRIPE_SECRET_API_KEY`, `PINSTRIPE_ADMIN_API_KEY`, `PINSTRIPE_MAX_RETRIES`, `PINSTRIPE_TIMEOUT_MS`. Flag any use of the unprefixed `SECRET_API_KEY` / `ADMIN_API_KEY` — those are the API server's env, and there is no fallback chain between the two families.
- Never declare a domain type here; they come through `src/types/contracts.types.ts` by `export type` from `@pinstripe/core/contracts`.
- Never import `sonner` or another toast library.
- Exactly one transport, in exactly one file. Flag a second HTTP client or a hand-written request function.
- Never set `splitting: false` in `tsup.config.ts` — `instanceof PinstripeError` breaks across entries.

Data-access layer. A call site must read like an English sentence without opening this file.

## Class and file
- One class per file, `{Resource}Repository`, matching the kebab-case singular filename. No `BaseRepository`, no `IRepository`, no module-level singleton.
- The constructor takes its data handle and nothing else. No logger.

## Method names — `<verb><Entity>`, entity always repeated
- Allowed: `create<Entity>`, `find<Entity>` (one, `| null`), `find<Entities>` (many), `upsert<Entity>`, `update<Entity>`, `delete<Entity>`, `count<Noun>`, `aggregate<Noun>`, or a real domain verb (`archiveInvoices`).
- Flag as required changes: `get*`, `list*`, `fetch*`, `load*`, `save*`, `insert*`, `add*`, `remove*`, `destroy*`, `purge*`, `exists*`; the suffixes `By<Field>`, `OrNull`, `OrThrow`, `Async`; and bare `find()` / `findOne()` / `findAll()`.
- The lookup key goes in the parameter name, not the method name: `findInvoice(id)`, never `findInvoiceById(id)`.

## Filters
- Exactly one `<Entity>Filters` interface per repository, declared and exported above the class, every field optional unless the query cannot run without it.
- Filter field names carry their operator: plural array = IN, `<field>Contains` = ILIKE, `from`/`to` = inclusive range, `beforeAt` / `<field>AfterAt` = exclusive bound.
- Build the where from conditional terms inside `and()` — it drops `undefined`. Flag any query-builder abstraction or specification DSL built on top of it.

## Returns
- The raw entity type Drizzle infers. No DTO, no response envelope, no formatted date. Flag a hand-written entity interface where `$inferSelect` exists.
- Missing is `| null`, never `undefined`. Normalise a destructured row with `?? null`; flag `rows[0]!`.
- Pure writes return `Promise<void>`; every method is `async` with an explicit `Promise<T>`.
- Sort is fixed per method, or one typed `sort: { field; order }` argument. Flag `sortBy` / `sortOrder` parameters.
- The repository knows `limit` and `offset`, never `page` and never `hasMore`.

## Errors
- Never throw `NotFoundError` here and never swallow a unique-key violation — the service maps both.
- Never log, and never import the app's HTTP error classes.

## Soft deletes
- Every read of a table with `deleted_at` filters it with `isNull(...)`. A missing filter is a high-severity finding: the deleted row reaches a customer.

Service layer: business logic, error decisions, and the shape the wire sees.

- The read verb states the outcome: `get<Entity>` throws `NotFoundError` when missing, `find<Entity>` returns `null`, `find<Entities>` returns `[]`. Flag `list*`, `get*OrNull`, `get*OrThrow`, and any `By<Field>` suffix.
- This is where `null` becomes an error. The repository returns `null`; the service decides which error class. Write it happy-path first: `if (entity) { return entity; }` then `throw new NotFoundError(...)` as the last statement — flag the negated guard shape.
- Map infrastructure failures at this boundary too: a unique-key violation becomes `ConflictError`, a `{Vendor}NotConfiguredError` becomes `ServiceUnavailableError`. Flag a driver or vendor error escaping unmapped.
- Pagination is the service's job: it converts `page` to `offset`, decides `hasMore`, and calls `count<Noun>` for the total.
- Never construct a repository or client here (`new XRepository(...)`) — they arrive from the composition root.
- Prefer a domain verb over a generic `update<X>` that actually archives, cancels, or finalizes something.
- Never build a cycle between two services.

Fastify routes. Handlers wire; they do not decide.

- Every route declares a `schema`. A route without one is a required change: the type provider hands the handler `unknown` and the reply is serialized by reflection.
- Routes are grouped by CALLER, not by domain — admin / system / management / public — each with its own prefix and its own `verify{Surface}Request` hook attached ONCE at the submodule's routes file. Flag a hook attached per route.
- A route that cannot use its submodule's hook must be an enumerated exception with its reason stated at the attachment site. Flag a silently unguarded route as a high-severity finding.
- A handler validates, calls exactly one service method, and replies through the shared envelope helpers (`success`, `created`, `paginated`, `noContent`). Flag domain branching, two repository calls orchestrated inline, an ad-hoc `reply.send({ ... })`, or a hand-written status code.
- Schema files: camelCase `{noun}Schema` variables, no `Body` / `Query` in the schema name, no intermediate sub-schemas composed from each other, no schema imported from another module's types file.

Fastify plugins are the seam between the environment and the application.

- File `{name}.plugin.ts` exporting `{name}Plugin`. Flag `register{Name}`.
- This is the ONLY place that reads `fastify.config`. Everything environment-shaped lives here: falling back from one variable to another, omitting credentials so the SDK picks up an instance role, choosing a provider by `NODE_ENV`. A client receives resolved config, never a variable name.
- No business logic and no HTTP error mapping in a plugin.
- Two plugins constructing the same client is two sources of configuration — flag it.
- Repositories and services are constructed once, in their registry plugin; the service registry registers last. Flag construction outside a registry.
- A plugin owning a connection calls `connect()` at registration and `close()` from an `onClose` hook — the client never calls either itself.

A client wraps exactly one third-party SDK connection.

- One primary class `{ClientName}Client` per file, matching the kebab-case `{name}.client.ts` filename, named after the SDK and not the role it plays. On a name collision, alias the vendor import — never rename our class.
- Constructor signature is always `(config, logger)`, config first. Destructure the config on the first line, then assign one field per line. Flag the logger folded into config, or config read field by field.
- Every field is `private` with a `_` prefix. Nothing public; expose the vendor handle through a read-only getter.
- Config is a `type` named `{ClientName}Config`. Options passed straight through keep the SDK's own type under a dedicated key — flag re-declared vendor options.
- Never accept the environment object, read `process.env`, or name an env variable inside a client.
- No I/O in the constructor, and the client never calls its own `connect()` / `close()`.
- A client that may be absent answers with `static isConfigured(config)`, not an instance getter.
- Errors: a `{Vendor}{Condition}Error` declared in this file, extending `Error` with an explicit `this.name`. Never import the app's HTTP error classes.
- Log through `this._logger` only, message `[<ClassName>] <method>() <message>`, errors at `error` level with `{ error }`. Flag `console` and free-form messages.
- Defaults are `SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE` constants at the top of the module, never inline magic numbers.
- New clients are re-exported from the layer's `index.ts`.

BullMQ producer and consumer sides, and the contract they share.

- Queue name, job names, payload types and `build*` helpers live in the shared `{name}.queue.ts` contract file only. Flag any queue or job name written as a string literal at a call site — a typo does not fail, the job is simply dispatched under a name nobody listens for.
- Constants: `*_QUEUE` and `*_JOB`, PascalCase values.
- Producer verb is `dispatch<X>` and it returns the job handle. Flag `enqueue*`, `queue*`, `schedule*`, `trigger*`.
- Producer connection sets `enableOfflineQueue: false`; worker connection sets `maxRetriesPerRequest: null`. Flag either missing — the second one kills the connection under normal idle behaviour.
- Consumer shapes: `{Name}Workflow` per queue, `{Job}Processor` with one public `handle(job)`, `private handle<Step>` helpers, `private static build<X>` pure helpers. Flag `*Consumer`, `*Runner`, `*Handler`.
- Boot order: validate config, resolve the workflow class from the registry, THEN open connections — constructing a workflow starts its worker.
- Shutdown order: mark unhealthy, `workflow.destroy()` (waits for active jobs), `context.destroy()`, close the health server. Flag tearing down the context first.
- A fire-and-forget write must be logged and its swallowing justified at the call site.

React components and forms.

## File and export
- PascalCase filename equal to the component name; exactly ONE default export and nothing else exported — no named exports, no exported constants, no exported props interface.
- Names: a Page or Modal is a task, `<Action><Domain>Page` / `<Action><Domain>Modal`; a collection page is the plural noun (`InvoicesPage`), never `…ListPage`. Every other component is `<Domain><Role>` with the role drawn from Layout / Card / Panel / Item / Actions / Form / Preview / Badge / Label / Button / Picker / Provider. Flag `Row`, `Entry`, `Box`, `Section`, `Wrapper`, `View`, `Screen`, `Container`.
- `{ComponentName}Props` is an `interface`, declared at the top of the file after imports, destructured at the signature, not exported.

## Handlers
- Callback props are `on*`; local handlers are `handleOn*` and pair with the prop they wrap. Subject before event: `onRoleChange` / `handleOnRoleChange`, never `handleOnChangeRole`. Flag `handleSave` (missing `On`) and a prop named `save` or `handleClose`.

## Forms
- `useForm` lives in the PAGE, never in the form component. The page owns the mutation hooks, `form.handleSubmit`, navigation, and the edit-mode `form.reset(...)`.
- The form component receives the whole `form: UseFormReturn<T>`, not individual fields, and triggers no mutation and no navigation.
- Fields are wrapped in a real `<form onSubmit>` with `preventDefault()`, primary action a native submit button. Flag submitting via `onClick`.
- Field arrays key on `field.id`, never the array index.
- `form.setValue` always passes `{ shouldDirty: true }`.
- The Zod schema stays private to the form config file; only the type, resolver and defaults are exported, and every message is user-facing.

## Layering
- A feature component never fetches data and never navigates — it takes callbacks. Flag a component calling a request function or a query hook directly.
- A Layout is a route shell and holds no logic.
- This app consumes `@pinstripe/sdk`: flag a reconstructed `api/` folder, a second HTTP client, or a hand-written request function. Toast is wired to the SDK provider's `onMutationError` / `onMutationSuccess` exactly once, in `apps/admin-ui/src/lib/pinstripe.tsx` — flag a second toast entry point.

PRECEDENCE: where these repo rules disagree with the built-in system rules above, these win. In particular this repo forbids ALL comments and JSDoc — never ask for an explanatory comment, and flag any comment that is not a tooling directive.

These apps consume `@pinstripe/sdk`. They do not build HTTP themselves.

- Flag any reconstruction of an `api/` folder, a second HTTP client, or a hand-written request function — `src/api/client.ts` and the `Request` / `Endpoint` / `Method` / `Params` / `Payload` / `Headers` setters were deleted on purpose.
- Data flows through the SDK's hooks. A component or effect calling a resource method directly has opted out of caching, dedup and the shared loading/error states.
- Toast is wired to the SDK provider's `onMutationError` / `onMutationSuccess` exactly once, in `apps/admin-ui/src/lib/pinstripe.tsx`. Flag a second toast entry point.
- Verb reminder: `list` / `retrieve` are correct only inside `packages/sdk/src/resources/**`. Elsewhere the kit verbs apply.

Repo-wide conventions. Report a violation as a required change, not a style nit — these are enforced rules, and the rule wins over the surrounding code.

## Comments
- No comments at all: no `//`, no `/* */`, no JSDoc. The only exception is a tooling directive (`eslint-disable-next-line`, `@ts-expect-error`). Flag commented-out code.

## Braces
- Every body is a braced block, however short — `if`, `for`, `while`, and arrow functions. An arrow function that produces a value uses an explicit `return`. Flag a concise arrow body (`(x) => x.id`) and an object literal returned through parentheses.

## Statements
- One statement, one job: read into a named local, blank line, then act. Flag `??`, a ternary, or an optional chain buried inside the argument of `throw`, `return`, or a call.
- Happy path first, conditions affirmative. Flag the shape `if (!token) { throw ... } return token;`.

## Optional reads
- Never write `?.` and `??` in the same expression, at ANY depth — `row?.total ?? 0` is in scope exactly as `a?.b?.c ?? []` is. In a package that ships lodash the form is `_.get(row, 'total', 0)`.
- Never walk the same optional path at two use sites; read it once into a named local with the default at the read.
- Never `length > 0` followed by `[0]`; take the first element and check it.
- The one allowed `??` is `?? null` at a boundary restating `undefined`.

## lodash
- Prefer `_.map(list, 'id')`, `_.filter(list, 'active')`, `_.reject(list, 'archived')`, `_.find(list, { id })`, `_.isEmpty(list)`, `_.keyBy`, `_.groupBy` over hand-rolled equivalents. Never pass an `async` iteratee to a lodash collection function — use `Promise.all` over a native map, or `for...of` when order matters.

## Naming
- Write DTO is `payload` in every layer; multi-condition read is `filters`; querystring DTO is `query`; route params are `params`; a caught error is `error` in `catch (error)` and `{ error }`. Flag `input`, `data`, `dto`, `body`, `err`, `req`, `res`, `cfg`, `ctx`, `idx`, `msg`.
- Flag `list*` as a verb anywhere outside `packages/sdk/src/resources/**`.
- A local names what it holds, not the step that produced it: `createdInvoice` / `existingInvoice`, never bare `created`, `existing`, `result`, `record`, `row`, `item`. A callback parameter takes the entity noun, never `x` or `el`.
- `delete` removes from a store, `remove` takes a member out of a collection, `destroy` ends a lifecycle. `close()` / `quit()` belong to something that had `connect()`.
- Booleans `is*` / `has*` / `should*`; timestamps `<verb>At`; collections a plain plural; maps `<nouns>By<Key>`.

## Types
- Never `any`, in a signature, a cast, or a generic argument — use `unknown` and narrow. A cast needs a reason a reader can check.
- Never write a type by hand that a schema, ORM or client already describes — derive it.
- Throw a named condition class, never a generic `Error` with a message callers pattern-match.
- A closed string set is a `<Name>Enum` plus a derived `` `${<Name>Enum}` `` union — flag a bare literal union or loose `export const` strings, and a raw string literal where an enum member exists.
- A nullable value is `T | null` through every layer. Flag `!`, flag `?? ''` / `?? 0` / a sentinel date, and flag `T | null | undefined`.

## Imports
- Inside a package that declares `paths`, never use `..` — use the alias. Relative paths only for the same folder or a subfolder, or inside a barrel.
- Never reach into another workspace package by file path; import what its `exports` expose.

## Constants
- A constant lives in the narrowest scope covering its use sites. Flag an exported const with one reader, or a file-level const read by one branch. No catch-all `constants.ts`.

## Logging
- `<function_name>() <message>` for a function, `[<ClassName>] <method_name>() <message>` inside a class. An error is logged at `error` level, the message ends in exactly `error`, and the cause goes under the key `error`. Flag free-form messages, `warn`/`info` for an error, `{ err }`, and variable data interpolated into the message.

## Minimal surface
- Flag an object rebuilt field by field when its shape already matches the return type, and a parameter or field no consumer reads.
